subject: Record resolved sword-strike seek distance
description: Nested Original commit `dd2e1c76217a3b64f8d69e2570823e874c6d284e` and outer Rust commit `036f6ea951ce40ab472b852b334561dac9e4b2b2` make future sword-strike input deterministic by recording the exact resolved seek tolerance. Original's simple-click `MOUSEWAYPATTERN_NONE` path emits command A but uses 90% of the weapon's generic maximum distance, while recognized A-E gestures use 90% of the selected thrust's maximum (`original-code/RHengine.cpp:15709-15730`, `15755-15778`, `15829-15861`; `original-code/RHSword.cpp:247-252`). The recorder now serializes `seek_distance` only for same-sector seeks; Rust carries the optional scalar through `TraceCommand`, `PlayerCommand`, macro capture, and macro replay, then consumes it verbatim when constructing the seek. Missing fields retain the historical strike-specific fallback, direct strikes normalize to `None`, and the parity native cache advances from v54 to v55. Live mouse resolution also includes Original's actor-target sector equality in `with_seek`; two existing actors with unassigned sectors remain equal just as two null C++ sector pointers do, while missing entities do not become same-sector accidentally. Focused coverage passes for resolved 63-unit versus legacy 54-unit application, two unassigned sectors, player-command and macro round trips including missing/direct fields, simple-click versus gesture distance calculation, trace normalization, and cache-version suffix consistency. `cargo check -p robin_rs --example original_parity_replay`, targeted rustfmt, and diff checks pass. This is a forward recording and replay-schema fix only. Task497 separately retires the old schema-12 nicouzouf Savegame_045 replay-014 capture whose command omitted the necessary provenance; this task does not claim that historical trace clears or matches EOF.
